title: Trace estimation for general symmetric matrices with Schatten-normalized error
summary: Estimate the trace $\tau=\operatorname{tr}(A)$ of a symmetric matrix.

task.description_zh: Estimate the trace $\tau=\operatorname{tr}(A)$ of a symmetric matrix.
description_paragraphs: Estimate the trace $\tau=\operatorname{tr}(A)$ of a symmetric matrix.

model.instance: The unknown input is an arbitrary real symmetric matrix $A\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$, possibly indefinite or zero. This specification imposes $1\le p\le2$.

assumptions.description: Positive semidefiniteness is not assumed; the spectrum may contain both signs.

model.parameter_domain_description: Assume $d\ge1$, $1\le p\le2$, $\epsilon>0$, and $0<\delta<1/2$, intersected with the shared MX_p parameter domain.
model.description_zh: The matrix satisfies $A=A^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ and may be indefinite or zero. The norm exponent satisfies $1\le p\le2$.
description_paragraphs: Assume $A=A^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$, allowing indefinite or zero matrices; the norm order is $1\le p\le2$.

operations.order_convention: Native linear action of the specified matrix; no derivative order of an unregistered scalar function is implied.

feedback_quality.description: Exact real vector responses, with no observation noise or rounding.

operations.coupling: Every query accesses the same fixed matrix; repeated queries are allowed.
operations.index_control: The algorithm selects vectors and an available channel; block width is charged by column.

oracle.query_domain_description: Right products map R^d to R^d, with only the listed right-product channel available. A q-column block costs q calls. Entries, inverse actions, shifted solves, and matrix-function actions are not free additional feedback.
oracle.description_zh: The quantity $d,p,\varepsilon,\delta$ is public and $A$ is hidden. Any $v\in\mathbb R^d$ returns exact $Av$; repeated and adaptive queries are allowed.
description_paragraphs: The information $d,p,\varepsilon,\delta$ is public and $A$ is hidden. Query $v\in\mathbb{R}^d$ returns exact $Av$. Repeated adaptive queries are allowed.

output.allowed_postprocessing: Arbitrary admissible postprocessing; the output need not have appeared as a query vector.
output.certificate_requirement: Only the true-loss guarantee is required; no computable certificate is requested.
output.description_zh: Return a scalar $\widehat\tau\in\mathbb R$; no additional certificate is required.
description_paragraphs: Return a scalar $\widehat\tau\in\mathbb{R}$; no additional certificate is required.

metric.normalization: If both numerator and denominator are zero, the loss is zero. A zero denominator with nonzero numerator gives +∞. Otherwise use the stated ratio.
metric.finiteness_conditions: The specified dimension is finite, and the model and spectral assumptions hold.
metric.description_zh: The success event is $|\widehat\tau-\operatorname{tr}(A)|\le\varepsilon\|A\|_{S_p}$, where $\|A\|_{S_p}=(\sum_i\sigma_i(A)^p)^{1/p}$. When $A=0$, the output must be zero. A general matrix can have zero trace and nonzero norm.
description_paragraphs: The success event is $|\widehat\tau-\operatorname{tr}(A)|\le\varepsilon\|A\|_{S_p}$, where $\|A\|_{S_p}=(\sum_i\sigma_i(A)^p)^{1/p}$. When $A=0$, the output must be zero. A general matrix can have zero trace and nonzero norm.

norms.definition: Euclidean vector norm $\|z\|_2=(\sum_i|z_i|^2)^{1/2}$ and matrix operator norm $\|M\|_{\rm op}=\max_{\|z\|_2=1}\|Mz\|_2$. Define $\|M\|_{S_p}=(\sum_i\sigma_i(M)^p)^{1/p}$; settings allowing p=infinity use $\|M\|_{S_\infty}=\|M\|_{\rm op}$.

proofs.title: Deterministic reconstruction using the standard basis, followed by free exact solution of the target task
proofs.body: Query all $d$ standard basis vectors, fixed before any response if nonadaptivity is required. These responses recover all columns. Summing their diagonal entries returns the exact trace. The argument applies to the stated matrix class, including zero trace, and uses $d$ right queries with deterministic success.

relations.error_map: For PSD matrices, $\|A\|_{S_1}=\operatorname{tr}(A)$, so relative trace error equals additive error normalized by the Schatten-one norm.

conditions: B=log A may be indefinite. A Bv call is not automatically free, and the error and target normalization must be checked again.
relations.error_map: The original trace error is $\epsilon\|\log A\|_{S_p}$. To make it at most $\eta$, use a known valid norm bound and a budget for simulation error.
relations.oracle_simulation: The action $Bv$ may be approximated by polynomials or Lanczos; it is not one exact $Av$ call. The included argument covers the SLQ quadratic-form route only.

components.cost: Each simulation costs the approximation degree for h = log. Trace upper and lower bounds do not transfer one for one.
